pr_title: liveshare test: only sleep if conn is nil
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/5338

- We only need to sleep if the `conn` is nil when attempting to connect, otherwise, we have a good connection and shouldn't take up execution time

issue_context.title: Flaky test: TestPortForwarderStart
issue_context.body:
```
go test -count 100 -timeout 5s -run '^TestPortForwarderStart$' github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/liveshare
```

It looks like the test times out here: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/31c6ba3807e6be436530d747715193ca0d69d1ef/pkg/liveshare/port_forwarder_test.go#L110-L110

/cc @bchuecos @josebalius https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/5270
comments: I'll take a look. @mislav curious did CI catch this? Wondering if we overlooked a failure before we merged?

The reason I ask is that this fails for me even without #5270. I am wondering how long it has been this way, and since this test makes heavy use of `net.Listen` to actually listen on a local port, I wonder if we are in contention to open/close the same port multiple times in fast succession.

Opened a PR that fixes this:

```
cli/pkg/liveshare git:jg/fix-flakey-test
❯ go test -count 100 -timeout 5s -run '^TestPortForwarderStart$'
PASS
ok      github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/liveshare     0.514s
```

review_comments:
Shouldn't this loop increment retries?

(Also: call it tries, since it's easier to understand the boundary condition.)

Also: why is the loop necessary? Under what circumstances does retrying DialTimeout succeed in a loop but fail if called once with a larger timeout? That seems like a bug. The only things that should cause DialTimeout to fail fast are intrinsic failures (e.g. bad arguments), not things that depend on the state of the network.

Gosh, this was a while ago so I can't remember the specifics, but I remember us discussing that there is an inherent race from the time that the port forwarder is started to the time it is available for connections. I think we had decided to implement this retry strategy to deal with this.

The retry increment is indeed missing.

Let's briefly record the motivation so that no-one cleverly simplifies it.

// We retry DialTimeout in a loop to deal with a race in PortForwarder startup.
